evidence.claim: The record for Rodolphe Sepulchre directly lists Dirk Aeyels in an Advisor field.
The record for Dirk Aeyels directly lists David L. Elliott in an Advisor field.
The University of Maryland explicitly names Dirk Aeyels among the academics advised by Elliott.
The record for David L. Elliott directly lists A. V. Balakrishnan in an Advisor field.
The repository states that Elliott completed this UCLA Ph.D. thesis in 1969 under A. V. Balakrishnan.
The record for A. V. Balakrishnan directly lists Ralph S. Phillips in an Advisor field.
The record for Ralph S. Phillips directly lists T. H. Hildebrandt in an Advisor field.
The record for T. H. Hildebrandt directly lists E. H. Moore in an Advisor field.
The record for E. H. Moore directly lists Hubert Anson Newton in an Advisor field.
The record for Hubert Anson Newton directly lists Michel Chasles in an Advisor field.

edges.note: The edge is in MGP, but Newton’s listed degree is a Yale B.A. and Chasles taught in Paris. This must not be rendered as a Yale doctorate or Yale B.A. supervision link.

chosen_layout.caption: A selected branch from the Mathematics Genealogy Project. Solid links mark doctoral supervision; dashed links mark historical teaching, mentorship or correspondence.
chosen_layout.compact_names_recent_to_older: Sepulchre ← Aeyels ← Elliott ← Balakrishnan ← Phillips ← Hildebrandt ← Moore ← H. A. Newton ← Chasles ← Poisson ← Lagrange ← Euler; Laplace is a second branch above Poisson.

limitations: This is a selected ancestry branch, not an exhaustive ancestry network. Euler and Laplace are deliberate display endpoints; MGP lists older ancestors beyond both.
MGP currently lists only Dirk Aeyels as Rodolphe Sepulchre’s advisor. This reports the database; it does not prove there were no additional institutional co-supervisors.

The complete displayed route is verified by direct MGP Advisor fields. It is not a continuous modern doctorate chain: the pre-Moore links include a B.A., historical school instruction and correspondence.

MGP labels Chasles (1814) and Poisson (1800) Ph.D. These historical records should be displayed with school and year plus the dashed-link legend; independently establishing modern-equivalent doctoral awards was outside scope.
The Chasles→Newton association must not be tied to Newton’s Yale B.A. date. MGP’s B.A. 1850 is degree metadata, not a verified date for studying with Chasles.
The degree label on Euler’s Basel 1726 record is blank. Lagrange’s Euler link is explicitly no degree; Lagrange’s separate B.A. 1754 belongs to Beccaria.
MGP is an ongoing, contributed database; all citations describe its records as retrieved, not independently inspected original diplomas.

additional_support.claim: Columbia-hosted genealogy independently reproduces the same Balakrishnan→Phillips→Hildebrandt→Moore→Newton→Chasles→Poisson→Lagrange→Euler chain.
UCLA’s obituary confirms Balakrishnan’s mathematics Ph.D. at USC in 1954.
Describes Chasles entering the École Polytechnique in 1812, interruption for the defence of Paris in 1814, and subsequent return to his studies; supports conservative historical-schooling treatment.
